messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a p99 jump in streaming for small prompts after last kernel switch. p95 pretty stable but p99 spiked.

matt: ugh, saw that in the dashboard this morning. numbers?

anya: quick snapshot from perf job: p95=380ms p99=1.1s for 8-token streaming responses. Before the kernel change p99 ~520ms. throughput barely changed.

ciara: is this specific to a model or quantization path?

anya: looks worst on q4_0 variants on A100s. xformers->custom-kernel change.

ravi: could be KV cache interaction. when we changed kernels we also altered the KV access pattern — lock hold times increased.

perfbot: perf-run-1955555555: model=redwood-lite-q4_0 region=us-west p95=380ms p99=1100ms microbatch=16 emit_interval_ms=40 kv_hit=0.87

matt: if kv_hit still high, why tail worse? maybe microbatch headroom + emit cadence causing bursts piling on.

ciara: hypothesis: kernel change increases per-token latency variance; with emit_interval small we expose variance as tail because microbatches wait to fill.

anya: yep. two levers to try: 1) increase emit cadence (emit_interval_ms -> 20) to reduce waiting? or actually decrease interval to emit earlier. 2) reduce microbatch max_tokens for streaming path so we avoid long waits.

ravi: careful: decreasing microbatch size hurts throughput/cost. need target SLO tradeoffs. we should measure p95/p99 delta vs tokens/sec.

matt: propose quick A/B: baseline (kernel=new, emit_interval_ms=40, microbatch_max_tokens=64) vs configA (emit_interval_ms=20, microbatch_max_tokens=64) vs configB (emit_interval_ms=40, microbatch_max_tokens=32). run 1h sweep with realistic arrival traces.

ciara: also add 'kernel_policy: latency_prefer' fallback to old kernel for canary traffic to confirm kernel is root cause.

anya: added. test matrix updated in test-plan gist: https://internal.gists/s/abcd1234

ravi: we should also capture per-request KV wait histograms. current logs only show aggregate kv_hit rate. need lock-hold ms histogram.

perfbot: telemetry-flag-on: kv_lock_histogram=true for job 1955555560

matt: small script to change config on Dedicated nodes:

```
# runtime override for canary
curl -X POST https://ops-api.local/runtime/override \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-q4_0","emit_interval_ms":20,"microbatch_max_tokens":64,"kernel_policy":"latency_prefer"}'
```

ciara: noted. I'll run the A/B at 10:30 PT and collect p50/p95/p99 + kv_lock_hpct + throughput.

anya: also instrument perceived-latency metric — time to first token delivered to client socket. that matters for UX.

ravi: good call. sometimes total completion times unchanged but first-byte latency improves and perception is better.

matt: if kernel variance the culprit, consider adding jitter to batching window so microbatch fills are less synchronized across cores (maybe reduce tail amplification).

ciara: we can prototype adaptive-windowing: base_emit_ms = 30, jitter +-10ms per worker. cheap to try.

anya: action items:
- ciara: run A/B sweep, collect histograms (assign)
- ravi: add kv_lock_histogram telemetry + analyse lock-hold distribution
- matt: add jittered-window patch to canary
- anya: coordinate rollout and prepare rollback plan (old kernel fallback)

ciara: on it. ETA 3h for first results.

deploy-bot: deploy started for runtime-canary (canary-42) — kernels: custom-kernel:v2, fallback: xformers:v1

matt: if p99 stays >800ms on configA/B, we revert kernel for streaming path only.

anya: thanks — want a short sync after results. :rocket:

ravi: ping me when histograms ready, I'll run the tail-hunt analysis script (tail-hunt.sh) and produce a short graph.

ciara: will post results here. keeping samples small (100-200 req/s) to isolate tail sources.

anya: TL;DR — regression likely from kernel -> KV lock interaction + microbatch alignment. experiments: emit interval, microbatch sizing, jitter, and kernel fallback.
